headline: World climate talks in Turkey end without a deal

sources.title: COP31 climate talks fail to reach deal amid fossil fuel and money rows (BBC)
Global climate summit collapses as countries fail to agree on moving away from fossil fuels (CNN)
Climate change talks fall apart in final hours over fossil fuels (NPR)
U.N. COP31 climate conference ends with no agreement after fossil fuel debate reaches standstill (CBS News)

chunks.text: On November 22, 2026, nearly 200 countries at a United Nations [[climate summit]] failed to agree on a main deal to fight climate change. Turkey hosted it on its [[southern coast]], and Australia led the [[negotiations]], or talks. The talks were due to {{wrap up}} on November 20. They {{dragged on}} for two more days, a record for these summits. They {{fell apart}} over two questions.

verbs.correct: To finish something, like a meeting
verbs.wrong: To pay the bill for a meeting
verbs.why: Our team meetings wrap up at noon on Fridays. The school play wraps up with a song from every class. The climate talks were due to wrap up on Friday, November 20, 2026.

verbs.wrong: To end with a group photo
verbs.why: Long meetings often drag on past dinner time. The rainy season sometimes drags on into June. The climate talks in Turkey dragged on for two more days.
Many plans fall apart when nobody agrees on money. Some business deals fall apart when one side asks for more. In the end, the climate talks fell apart over fossil fuels and money.

chunks.text: The first was [[fossil fuels]]: coal, oil and gas. Burning them is the main cause of [[global warming]]. An early version of the deal said the world should {{phase out}} fossil fuels, or slowly stop using them. Some [[oil-producing countries]] {{pushed back}}. Russia, one of them, said dropping these fuels fast would make energy too expensive. Later versions {{left out}} the words "fossil fuels." So the European Union and Pacific island nations [[rejected]] the final version. The European Union's two lead [[officials]] {{walked out}}, one report said.

verbs.wrong: To give something a new name
verbs.why: Many cities phase out old buses over several years. Some schools phase out paper books and use tablets. An early version of the deal said the world should phase out fossil fuels.

verbs.wrong: To grow food for the summit
verbs.why: Workers often push back when a company cuts their pay. Parents push back when a school plans longer days. Some oil-producing countries pushed back against the early version.
Short news reports often leave out small details. My recipe leaves out sugar for a healthier cake. Later versions of the deal left out any mention of fossil fuels.

verbs.correct: To leave a meeting to show you disagree
verbs.wrong: To become a new member country
verbs.why: Some workers walk out of a meeting when they feel ignored. Students sometimes walk out of class to protest a new rule. The European Union's two lead officials walked out over the final version.

chunks.text: The second was money. Poorer countries face more [[heat waves]] and [[droughts]], long periods with no rain. They wanted rich countries to {{step up}} and pay to help them [[adapt]] to hotter weather. At the 2025 summit, countries agreed to [[triple]] that money. But the final version gave no clear numbers. Every country must agree on a deal, a rule called [[consensus]]. So if even one country {{holds out}}, there is no deal. The talks last failed like this in 2009.

verbs.why: Neighbors often step up when a family needs help. Big companies step up after a storm with food and water. Poorer countries wanted rich countries to step up and pay to help them adapt.

verbs.correct: To keep saying no to a deal
verbs.wrong: To sign a deal for others
verbs.why: Some workers hold out for better pay before they sign a contract. A few buyers hold out until the price drops. At these summits, if even one country holds out, there is no deal.

chunks.text: The head of the United Nations said he was "[[deeply disappointed]]." Countries still made progress on smaller plans, such as help for workers as countries move to [[clean energy]]. The United Nations' top climate official said he would {{look into}} changing how the summits make decisions. He said they have had problems before and {{come back}} stronger. The next summit is in Ethiopia in November 2027.

verbs.why: The city looks into every complaint about noisy roads. My doctor looks into the reason when I feel tired. The United Nations' top climate official said he would look into changing how the summits make decisions.

verbs.correct: To recover after a hard time
verbs.why: Many small towns come back after a big flood. Some sports teams come back stronger after a bad year. The climate official said the summits have had problems before and come back stronger.

mainIdea.s: Nearly 200 countries at a United Nations climate summit in Turkey could not agree on a main deal. They were split over coal, oil and gas, and over money for poorer countries.
mainIdea.why: The talks fell apart over two questions. Some oil-producing countries pushed back on a plan to stop using fossil fuels, and poorer countries wanted rich countries to step up with money.

mainIdea.s: The climate deal in Turkey failed because rich nations refused to mention fossil fuels. Angry oil-producing nations then walked out of the room at the final meeting.
mainIdea.why: Close, but some oil-producing countries were the ones who pushed back. The European Union's two lead officials walked out because the final version left out fossil fuels.

mainIdea.s: Turkey opened a large new solar power plant on its southern coast in November. The government says the plant will send clean electricity to about one million homes.
mainIdea.why: This story is about climate talks that failed. Nearly 200 countries could not agree on a main deal after the talks dragged on for two more days.

tf.s: The climate talks in Turkey fell apart without a main deal.
tf.why: Nearly 200 countries failed to agree on a main deal, so the talks ended with no agreement on the biggest questions.

tf.s: The talks wrapped up early, before their planned last day.
tf.why: The talks were due to finish on Friday, November 20, but they dragged on for two more days.

tf.s: The final version of the deal asked the world to phase out fossil fuels.
tf.why: Only an early version said that. Some oil-producing countries pushed back, and later versions left out the words completely.

tf.s: The European Union rejected the final version of the deal.
tf.why: The European Union and Pacific island nations said no to it, and the European Union's two lead officials walked out.

tf.s: Poorer countries wanted rich countries to step up with money.
tf.why: They wanted money to help them adapt to hotter weather, but the final version gave no clear numbers.

tf.s: One country alone cannot stop a deal at these summits.
tf.why: Every country must agree on a deal, a rule called consensus. If even one country holds out, there is no deal.

lines.text: Did you hear about the climate summit in Turkey?
Yes. Nearly 200 countries were there, but the talks {{fell apart}}, right?
Right. They were supposed to {{wrap up}} on Friday, but they {{dragged on}} until Sunday.
Wow. Why were they so [[at odds]]?
Mostly fossil fuels. An early version of the deal said the world should {{phase out}} coal, oil and gas.
Let me guess. Some of the big oil-producing countries {{pushed back}}.
Exactly. So the later versions {{left out}} the words "fossil fuels" completely.
How did Europe react to that?
The EU rejected the final version, and its two lead officials {{walked out}} of the room.
So both sides [[stuck to their guns]].
Pretty much. There was a lot of [[back and forth]] about money, too.
Poorer countries wanted rich countries to {{step up}} and help them adapt to hotter weather.
But one country can't block everything, can it?
Actually, it can. Every country has to agree, so if even one {{holds out}}, there's no deal.
So the talks really [[hit a wall]].
They did. The UN climate chief said he'd {{look into}} changing how the summits make decisions.
Sounds like it's [[back to the drawing board]] before the next summit in Ethiopia.
